value.title: typing grace gate — hold delivery while a human is typing
value.summary: Pushed messages to omp/pi seats are held while the human has typed within PIJ_TYPING_GRACE_MS (default 60 s) and delivered once idle; the hold is visible from both ends and control commands bypass it. Claude/send-keys seats move their veto from 'draft present' to the same recent-keystroke rule, retiring plan 134's AC7 pathology.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Jordan 2026-09-05: 'pij messages to omp seats step on me if I'm already typing. Detect if I typed in the client in the last 1 min and delay; if I don't type for 1 min then step on is fine.' Plan 134 removed the composer veto for omp/pi entirely (extension-stream, delivered 0 s) and left Claude seats keyed on DRAFT PRESENT (queued/human-typing + draft sha), which is what produced 8 min at attempt 101. Recency-of-keystroke is the fact we care about; draft-present was the nearest observable. Design: the pij extension is in-process for omp/pi and can hook editor changes directly (`editor.onChange` → lastEditAt); RustRuntimeSession.consumePushed claims a pushed row, and if now−lastEditAt < grace it HOLDS (not acked, not injected), shows `⏸ N held · typing` in the status line, reports the hold to the daemon so `pij state`/tail show `held/human-typing since <t>`, and injects+acks when idle ≥ grace. Control commands (compact/new/reload) and messages flagged urgent bypass. Claude seats: the interaction gate in crates/harnesses keeps the `human-typing` word but derives it from keystroke recency (pane-signals) with the same grace, so a parked draft stops blocking after one grace. No hard cap (Jordan's rule); observability is the cap. Evidence base vendored: assets/inputs/plan-134-live-proof.md, plan-134-ac-rows.md.

sections.name: goals
value: omp/pi: a pushed message is held while a keystroke happened in the last grace window and delivered within one grace of the last keystroke; order preserved; nothing lost across /new or a daemon restart (held = unacked).
Both ends can see a hold: recipient status line and sender-visible `pij state <seat>` / tail event with reason and since-timestamp.
Control commands and urgent messages bypass the hold.
Claude/send-keys seats: `human-typing` means keystroke within grace, not draft present — closes plan 134 AC7's failure mode with a bounded, observable rule.
One knob: PIJ_TYPING_GRACE_MS (default 60000), read by both runtimes from one definition.

sections.name: non_goals
value: A maximum hold time (Jordan: no cap; visibility is the control).
Changing the send-keys transport itself or the UDS socket path for Claude seats.
Reaping/tombstoning seats; Copilot native extension delivery (plan 137 owns the delivery/mod.rs match arm).

value.claim: omp hold then deliver within one grace of the last keystroke
value.text: LIVE: type into an omp seat's composer at t0 (no Enter); `pij send` at t0+5 s → recipient shows `⏸ 1 held`, nothing injected; stop typing → the message is injected at t0+60 s ±3 s. Unit: fake clock test in the extension asserts hold at 59 s and inject at 60 s. Paste both.
value.receipt: LIVE, seat pij-selective-blackbird (omp): last keystroke t0=1788573861190, send at t0+5.09s, spine seq 9308 delivery.held {reason:human-typing, since_ms:1788573861113} with no injection and no ack; typing stopped; seq 9326 delivery.released at t0+60.7s and seq 9328 delivery.inbox-ack outcome=reader-read. Inside the +/-3s allowed. World-B control on the same rig injected at t0+6.1s and destroyed the draft. Unit: fake-clock hold at 59s / release at 60s in rust-runtime.test.ts. assets/live-proof.md.

value.claim: a parked draft no longer blocks after one grace
value.text: LIVE omp: type a draft, leave it unsubmitted, wait 61 s, send → delivered (injected) despite non-empty composer. CONTROL on main first shows today's immediate injection (no hold at all) so the test discriminates by content: hold observed in world A, not in world B.
value.receipt: LIVE, seat pij-glorious-bobolink (omp): draft typed then left alone 68.1s; send at 1788574528604; spine seq 9517 message.pushed, 9519 delivery.released, 9520 delivery.inbox-ack — delivered 590ms later with a NON-EMPTY composer and no hold. Control on main first (assets/live-proof.md control B1) showed immediate injection while the human was mid-sentence, so the two worlds discriminate by WHEN, not by whether.

value.claim: the hold is visible from both ends
value.text: While held: omp status line shows `⏸ N held · typing`; `pij state <seat>` (and `pij-rs tail`) show a `delivery.held` row with reason=human-typing, msg_id and since; on release a `delivery.released` row. Paste rows. RECEIPT CLAUSE AMENDED 2026-09-05 (prime ruling on PM evidence): the push receipt is ALREADY queued/reason=extension-stream until the extension acks on main — crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:249-251 routes Omp|Pi to DeliveryRung::Observe and :397-398 emits Queued{reason:'extension-stream'}, flipping to delivered only on delivery.inbox-ack. No behaviour change is required: u2 ships a REGRESSION GUARD test pinning queued-before-ack / delivered-after-ack and leaves delivery/mod.rs untouched (which also retires the plan-137 baton).
value.receipt: LIVE both ends: recipient status line captured while held reads '⏸ 1 held · typing'; sender-side `pij-rs state pij-glorious-bobolink --json` carries held[] with msg_id/reason/since_ms for all three held rows; spine carries delivery.held then delivery.released per message. Receipt clause amended before implementation (prime ruling): the extension-stream push receipt was ALREADY queued-until-ack on main (delivery/mod.rs:249-251, :397-398), so u2 shipped a regression guard, proven non-vacuous by a mutation control (lying producer -> delivered vs queued, reverted, git status clean).

value.text: With a hold active, `pij send <seat> --command compact` (and new/reload) is injected immediately; a normal message queued behind it stays held. Unit test + live paste.
value.receipt: UNCHECKED BY RULING (prime, on PM evidence): the bypass guard is correct and STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE in production, so it is not ticked on unit evidence. (1) the rs CLI refuses the command form by design — 'rs cannot serve pij send <id> --command <name>: a control command is a different act from a message... deliberately left on legacy'; (2) crates/core/src/model.rs Msg has NO urgent field (hits only in TypeScript); (3) /v1/send hardcodes command: None (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1237). rust-runtime.ts:401 therefore checks fields the live daemon can never populate. Unit tests cover both bypass branches. Practical consequence: today a compact/new/reload aimed at a typing omp seat waits up to one grace. Follow-up plan minted by prime after 136 closes.

value.text: Kill the omp process while 2 messages are held → after restart/re-register both are redelivered in order (daemon rows were never acked). Daemon restart while held → same. Paste spine rows.
value.receipt: LIVE, seat pij-glorious-bobolink: three rows held, then kill -9 on the omp process (pid 9999). Rows survived as state=pending attempt=0 — held really is unacked and unclaimed. A new process re-registered as the same seat; the recipient itself reported 'Received in order: AC1B-136: held on main's binary; AC5-136-FIRST; AC5-136-SECOND' and all three jobs went done/acked_at=1788574286. Ordering is not luck: Queue::claim orders only ELIGIBLE rows, so u1's witness reproduced the [newer, older] inversion before the session_start peek->release->claim recovery loop closed it.

value.text: LIVE Claude seat: draft typed then idle 61 s -> delivered (was: queued/human-typing indefinitely, plan 134 EEE16F98 shape); an edit 5 s ago -> queued/human-typing with next_retry_at <= grace. Interaction-gate unit tests updated; the old draft-present-forever behaviour has a RED control. WORDING AMENDED 2026-09-05 (prime ruling on u3's assumption 1): the gate's evidence is OBSERVED EDIT RECENCY — composer content sampled at the pane observer's 600 ms interval — not raw key events, so a keypress that changes nothing observable (arrow keys, a menu) does not refresh the grace. The plan said 'keystroke' and the implementation honestly cannot see keystrokes; the claim is narrowed to what the instrument actually measures rather than the code being credited with more than it does.
value.receipt: LIVE on a socket-resolvable Claude seat (pij-dear-primate, /tmp/cc-socks/76368.sock, pid matches the row). (a) A draft parked since ~09:35 — hours — delivered: spine seq 9484 outcome delivered/origin=injected-to-transport over claude-uds, WITH THE DRAFT STILL IN THE COMPOSER. World-B control refused the identical scenario for 200+s (control B2), which is plan 134's AC7 pathology retired. (b) An edit 5s before the send: seq 9489 queued/reason=human-typing/draft_sha=825fdcf649aa. Caveat recorded: next_retry_at is 0 rather than last_edit+grace (satisfies '<= grace' literally); threading the bounded value needs delivery/mod.rs, which plan 137 owns. The old draft-present-forever test has a rewritten RED control in crates/harnesses, and a second obsolete control (pointer worker) was retired at composition.

value.text: PIJ_TYPING_GRACE_MS default 60000 lives in one place (crates/core delivery vocabulary) and the extension reads it from the daemon (/v1/config or the register response, additive) rather than restating the number; a test on each side asserts the value it observed.
value.receipt: ONE definition, verified by grep on the composed tree: `pub const DEFAULT_TYPING_GRACE_MS: u64 = 60_000` at crates/core/src/delivery.rs:13 is the only Rust grace literal (config.rs:163's 60_000 is interaction_idle_ms, a different setting deliberately kept separate). The daemon reads the PIJ_TYPING_GRACE_MS override in exactly ONE function, http::resolve_typing_grace_ms, shared by the register response and the interaction gate — composed by the PM, because u2 and u3 had each honestly resolved it on their own side and two resolutions of one env var is two numbers nobody chose. TypeScript has exactly one occurrence: `accepted.typing_grace_ms ?? 60000` at rust-runtime.ts:166, and a test asserts the wire value WINS over that fallback.

value.text: cargo test/clippy/fmt, bun test, harness checks green on the composed branch; every new behavioural test shows a pasted RED on the pre-fix tree.
value.receipt: `harness checks` 8/8 PASS with none skipped on the composed branch (02:22:21Z, envelope /tmp/pij-136-gate4.json, copied to assets/observations/pij-136-gate4.json); cargo test --workspace, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings and cargo fmt --check all clean. RED-first witnesses pasted per unit in assets/observations/ (u1 seven original + composition/FIFO/single-release REDs; u3's rewritten forever-veto control; u2's http/route REDs). Two exceptions ruled honestly rather than faked: a brand-new module has no behavioural RED (u1's HoldQueue is GREEN-on-new-code, provenance carried by the runtime witnesses), and a regression guard for already-correct behaviour was proven non-vacuous by a mutation control instead of a false RED. Toolchain OBSERVED, not pinned: cargo 1.98.0, rustc 1.95.0 (Homebrew), clippy 0.1.98, rustup absent.

value.title: Contract, three units, compose, live
value.name: u0 contract → u1 ext ∥ u2 daemon ∥ u3 gate → compose
value.brief: Freeze the hold/release event shape + grace source (u0, PM); fan out u1 (TS extension sensor+hold queue), u2 (Rust daemon: held/released rows, grace exposure, honest push receipt), u3 (Rust interaction gate recency); compose; live proofs.
value.receipt: All five tasks checked with receipts. Composed, merged to main (be778b9c, then 1142c87e, 677c118b and 6f5d33c6 for the delta, u5 and the review remediation), with harness checks 8/8 green at every gate and the live proofs in assets/live-proof.md. Cross-model review: APPROVE WITH FINDINGS, 13 findings, all dispositioned — f1 struck after a live single-release proof, f2/f3/f10/f11 fixed in ae427e2d, and one follow-up left deliberately open with its problem statement written down (a failed hold leaves the row claimed-and-running, so its five frame retries cannot succeed while the seat's serial key is held by that same claim). 7 of 8 ACs proven live; AC4 recorded unreachable rather than ticked on unit evidence.
